items.title: Archer Aviation Drops 6%, EHang Slides 7%, Joby Falls 5%: Is Cathie Wood Right to Keep Buying Air Taxi Stocks?
items.summary: Cathie Wood keeps buying Archer while its stock bleeds, and the cash clock is ticking louder than the rotors. Can her patience outlast the burn, or will dilution settle the argument first?

items.title: Stock Market Today: Dow, Nasdaq Dive As Chips Tumble; Trump Says This On Huang, Lutnick (Live Coverage)
items.summary: The Dow Jones index falls. President Trump speaks on Nvidia, Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick. Chip plays skid.

items.title: Cathie Wood Buys Archer, Down More Than 40% in 2026. Is Joby the Better Air Taxi Bet?
items.summary: Cathie Wood keeps buying a stock that has lost more than half its value this year, while its bigger-cash rival has fallen even harder. Neither has flown a paying passenger, and one still has a milestone to hit.

items.title: A high-stakes week for tech: Anthropic IPO and Nvidia earnings
items.summary:
Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi previews a huge week for the tech market, with Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) set to file for its IPO and Nvidia (NVDA) set to deliver its earnings call as investors brace for results. 

Sozzi sits down for a 1-on-1 with Cisco (CSCO) CEO Chuck Robbins to look at the state of the tech market, Q1 earnings, and the company's growth.

items.title: Why Starship's breakthrough could give SpaceX a massive edge
items.summary:
SpaceX (SPCX) had a major breakthrough during its Starship launch over the weekend. 

Barron's associate editor Al Root joins "The 8:30" hosts Julie Hyman and Pras Subramanian to discuss what the launch means for SpaceX and the broader space industry.

items.title: Vulcan Rocket Mishap Hurts Amazon’s Satellite Aspirations
items.summary: SpaceX’s launch capacity and reliability is a huge competitive advantage.

items.title: Lies, spies and sex are just one part of the Nvidia story. The real stakes are much bigger
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company he founded this week after reports of multiple affairs, including one with a subordinate and one with a woman whom US officials feared could be working with Chinese intelligence.

items.title: Amazon Just Lost 40 Leo Satellites. The Bigger Problem Is the Rocket It Booked 38 Launches On
items.summary: Forty satellites vanished in minutes, yet Wall Street barely blinked. The real damage sits in a launch schedule with few backup rockets, a 2029 regulatory clock, and a rival that happens to be one of Amazon's own launch providers.
